strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas rolling covariance/correlation accuracy bug (GH#66678 / PR#66678) where incremental accumulators become poisoned after a large/outlier/large-offset value leaves the rolling window, leading to wrong results and sometimes NaNs for later windows. Use the project’s own failing regression test `test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan` (and optionally the oracle-based tests around it) so the buggy revision fails and the fixed revision passes.

build_commands: python -m pip install cython numpy python-dateutil tzdata pytest
pinned_because: NumPy is numerically relevant; the defect is float64 accuracy. The exact NumPy version can matter for bit-level comparisons, so keep it consistent across buggy and fixed runs.
Cython is required to build pandas from source; the failing code path lives in pandas’ cythonized window internals.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision, `test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan` fails because the rolling `cov`/`corr` results for windows at/after `window-1` become NaN (or differ from the expected two-pass (np.cov/np.corrcoef) values beyond the test’s tolerance). On the fixed revision (PR#66678 merged commit), the same test passes: no NaNs appear in `result.iloc[window-1:]` and the full series matches the recomputed oracle with the test’s tolerances.
strategy.numerical_probe: NaN poisoning or silent accumulator drift after the large ±1e12 value leaves the rolling window; specifically in `calc_corr` a negative ssqdm_x can cause sqrt-of-negative -> NaN, and separately incremental cov/corr accumulators can become silently wrong for later windows.
risks: Platform/toolchain dependency: pandas window accuracy issues may be sensitive to CPU/BLAS/extended precision; run on the same architecture (x86_64/ARM64) and OS for both revisions.
Build config dependency: ensure both revisions are built with the same compiler and flags; C-extension build differences could change floating-point behavior.

Dependency/version sensitivity: although the strategy does not require pinned versions, NumPy float64 math and any BLAS-linked behavior can affect exact ulp-level results; keep NumPy version identical across buggy and fixed runs.

Not all environments will reliably hit the NaN-then-poisoning mode; using the exact test `test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan` is preferred because it asserts `not result.iloc[window-1:].isna().any()`.

The test diff also introduces additional oracle-based tests (`test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit` and `test_rolling_cov_corr_shared_offset`) that compute expected values using `np.cov`/`np.corrcoef` and may be more robust than the no-NaN-only check; if only silent error (not NaNs) occurs, the full `tm.assert_series_equal` portion of `test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan` should still fail.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-5, atol=0 for the assert_series_equal portion of `test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan`
oracle.reference_source: The test computes expected rolling values using a two-pass oracle: for each window it calls `np.cov` (method='cov') or `np.corrcoef` (method='corr') on deviations recentered by `chunk_x[0]`/`chunk_y[0]` (translation-invariant) and asserts the resulting full Series.
oracle.why: The oracle in this specific test is independent of pandas’ incremental accumulator implementation; it recomputes each rolling window from scratch.

fails_on_buggy.description: The assertion that fails can be either (a) `assert not result.iloc[window - 1 :].isna().any()` due to NaNs in later windows, because incremental accumulators lead to negative ssqdm_x and `calc_corr` takes sqrt of a negative; or (b) the subsequent `tm.assert_series_equal(..., rtol=1e-5, atol=0)` because even if NaNs are absent, later windows are silently wrong after the large value leaves the window.
fails_on_buggy.expected: After the large ±1e12 exits (in this test, for window=3 the large values are at indices 2 and 3), `result` is not equal to the two-pass oracle within the test tolerance.

passes_on_fixed.description: All later windows match the two-pass oracle within `rtol=1e-5, atol=0`, and `result.iloc[window-1:]` contains no NaNs (for both `method in ['cov','corr']`).
